classificationRules: automated_real_interaction: a browser test reaches the action through the control a person sees (click, tap, keyboard, navigation) AND asserts the user-observable outcome; mutating actions must also assert persistence after reload/navigation.

Playwright fill() into a plain visible text/tel/number/textarea field counts as real typing (fill() requires the element to be visible, enabled and editable, and focuses it). fill() does NOT count for native-picker controls (date, select, file) or any control whose visible affordance is a different element from the DOM control (e.g. the opacity-0 date input under the due-date display).

automated_partial: the test uses page.goto to skip the in-app entry point, fill() on a picker control, page.request/API calls, page.evaluate fetch, stubs/mocks, component tests with fireEvent, or asserts only rendering (screenshots, axe scans, text presence).

A test that is test.skip()-ed or test.fixme()-ed in a project does not count for that project; a test.fail()-annotated (expected-failure) test never counts as coverage. `npm run coverage:journeys` enforces this: every titled reference must be a test Playwright itself registers (`playwright test --list`), and each claimed project needs a real test that its AST shows is not skipped, fixme'd or expected to fail there; a condition it cannot evaluate does not count. With `--results <playwright-json>` it also checks the claims against an actual run: CI does this for the @critical run on every PR, and the separate `Journey coverage (full)` workflow does it for every real claim (`--require-results`).
tests/ux-audit specs run in the CI ux-audit job, which is report-gated (scripts/ux-audit.ts), not a per-test exit-code gate; they are credited but called out as such.

A P0/P1 action that is not `automated_real_interaction` or `manual_verified`, or that still carries a manual check, must have an entry in the exception register (`exceptions` in the inventory): its category, why it is not fully automated, whether it blocks a release, the evidence a release needs, and whether an automation strategy exists. `npm run coverage:journeys` fails when an entry is missing, stale, or contradicts the action's status.

findings.summary: Blocked-popup detection never works: invoice detail (sendWhatsApp) and the Beranda queue (openReminder) call window.open(href, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer') and treat a null return as 'blocked', but the HTML spec makes window.open() return null whenever noopener is set. So after WhatsApp opens normally, a 'Buka WhatsApp' fallback link still appears (a second click opens a second chat), and a really blocked popup is indistinguishable.
findings.status: fixed: PR #29 (merge ac53043, into staging 2026-10-07; not yet on main/Production). Regression: e2e/home/follow-up-queue.spec.ts and e2e/invoices/overdue-invoice.spec.ts (popup opened -> one tab, no fallback), e2e/whatsapp/popup-blocker.spec.ts (real Chromium blocker -> fallback, no tab). findings.summary: Any change to a deal that did not itself name a stage moved the deal back to Masuk and wrote a '<stage> → Masuk' entry into its history: saving the contact name on deal detail, and repairing the WhatsApp number on deal detail, on invoice detail (Simpan & kirim) or in the Beranda queue. Cause: dealPatchSchema was dealInputSchema.partial(), and zod's partial() keeps the create schema's status default ('MASUK'), so every PATCH /api/deals/:id without a status carried status MASUK. The page kept showing the old stage until its next load. The schema line dates from the M1 slice (65393b6, 2026-07-14, on main). The first screen that sent such a PATCH was the Beranda queue repair (7633904, 2026-08-09); the contact name and the deal-detail repair came with T-17 (f696973, 2026-08-23), which also introduced the stage history. All of it is on main/Production. Found 2026-10-11 by the first DEAL-DETAIL-02 journey (stage read after a reload on a Nego deal); the earlier unit test used a deal already at Masuk and the contact-repair journey did not read the stage.
findings.status: fixed: fix/deal-patch-keeps-stage-2026-10-11 (into staging; not yet on main/Production). The patch schema now has no status default, so a patch changes only what it names. Regression: src/lib/deal-validation.test.ts, src/lib/deals.test.ts (every non-Masuk stage x four patch shapes), e2e/deals/patch-keeps-stage.spec.ts (contact name on a Nego deal; number repaired from invoice detail on an Invoice deal), e2e/deals/contact-repair.spec.ts (stage and history asserted). The Beranda queue's repair has no browser regression (HOME-04 stays partial); it is covered at repository level by src/lib/deals.test.ts. Stored rows are not repaired: deals already moved to Masuk this way stay there. A deal reset since T-17 has a '→ Masuk' history entry at the time of the edit; a Beranda repair between 2026-08-09 and T-17 left no history entry, so a count of such transitions is a lower bound. That read-only Production count needs Chris. Still open in the same schema, not reached by any screen: a PATCH with feeIdr null or '' stores 0, and deadline null stores 1970-01-01 (z.coerce).

findings.summary: A saved contact name cannot be removed on deal detail. Emptying the field and pressing Simpan sends an empty PATCH body (contactName || undefined), the page answers 'Nama kontak disimpan', and the old name is put back in the field and is still there after a reload. Verified in the browser 2026-10-11.
findings.status: open, triaged 2026-10-11: recommended P3 (low), fix after the release, not a release blocker. Nothing is lost or corrupted and nothing is shown to a recipient; the cost is a wrong name the owner cannot remove and a 'Nama kontak disimpan' message that is not true. Recommended behaviour: an emptied field clears the name (send contactName: null and accept null in dealPatchSchema), with a browser regression test asserting the cleared value after reload. Repro: deal detail of any deal with a contact name -> empty 'Nama kontak' -> Simpan -> 'Nama kontak disimpan' -> the old name is back in the field and after a reload. Not changed here (outside this work's scope). No browser test asserts either behaviour.

findings.summary: The route error card's Coba lagi never recovered from a failed server render. src/app/(app)/error.tsx called reset(), which in this Next.js version (16.3) only re-renders what the browser already holds, i.e. the same failure; the documented way to ask the server again is retry(). After the cause was gone the button still left 'Gagal memuat.' on screen and sent no request; only a manual reload helped. Found 2026-10-11 by the first NAV-08 journey, the first test to make a server component really fail and then recover.
